title: Automated Inventory Reconciliation for Retail Logistics
business: A regional logistics provider managing thousands of daily inventory updates across disparate warehouse management systems.
problem: The company faces significant data silos where inventory records in legacy on-premises databases fail to synchronize with cloud-based order management systems, leading to frequent stock-outs and inaccurate fulfillment reporting.
solution: AWS Glue provides a serverless data integration platform that allows the logistics provider to catalog disparate data sources and execute ETL jobs to normalize inventory schemas into a unified data lake format, ensuring consistency across systems without managing infrastructure.
steps: Define metadata tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog by crawling existing on-premises and cloud database endpoints.
Develop ETL scripts using the AWS Glue visual interface or Python shell to map heterogeneous source fields to a standardized schema.
Schedule Glue triggers to execute transformation jobs periodically, ensuring the data lake remains current with warehouse updates.
Configure the Glue job to write the transformed output into an Amazon S3 bucket for consumption by downstream analytics tools.
outcome: The organization achieves a single source of truth for inventory levels, enabling real-time visibility into stock availability and reducing manual reconciliation efforts.
limitation: AWS Glue jobs are subject to cold start latency during initial container provisioning; users can check this by monitoring the 'Job Run Time' metrics in the Glue console to determine if the overhead impacts time-sensitive synchronization requirements.
